key_insight: Reliable evaluation of engineered surfaces requires hierarchical, multi-modal NDE that matches inspection physics to surface and interface defects.
engineering_relevance: Combining rapid screening with calibrated confirmation can support inspection of coatings, cold-sprayed deposits, laser-clad overlays, and additively manufactured surface regions.
method: Review NDE capabilities and limitations for thickness, adhesion, residual stress, porosity, and debonding.
Match electromagnetic, thermal, ultrasonic, optical, and X-ray methods to inspection needs.
Assess in-process sensing, data fusion, physics-informed machine learning, and digital twins.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a qualitative review of inspection methods and identifies limited probability-of-detection evidence rather than reporting new quantitative validation.
watch_item: Deployment remains constrained by scarce reference specimens, incomplete acceptance criteria, and poor transferability of data-driven models.
paper_title: Non-Destructive Evaluation for Engineered Surfaces: Methods, In-Process Sensing, and Data-Driven Inspection in the NDE 4.0 Era
